fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Aaron lays both hands on the live goat's head and confesses over it “…all the iniquities and rebellious acts of the Israelites in regard to all their sins.” (Leviticus 16:21). Then a man appointed for the task sends the goat away, and it carries those sins into a solitary place (Leviticus 16:22). I think those hands stay on that goat a while, because that's a lot of confessing.

That's right, baker. The man who released the goat “…must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water; afterward he may reenter the camp.” (Leviticus 16:26). Clothes first, bath too, and only THEN the camp. He walked a goat into the wilderness, and the camp is not about to take his word that he's clean. I've gotten dough all over this mustache and still just got a rag.

No days are counted here, friend. The man “…must wash his clothes and bathe himself with water; afterward he may reenter the camp.” (Leviticus 16:26). Seven days outside sounds like a whole camping trip for one goat errand. Here it's a wash, a bath, and he's back in.

You got it, baker. The bull and the goat, whose blood was brought into the Most Holy Place, are taken outside the camp, “and their hides, flesh, and dung must be burned up.” (Leviticus 16:27). Hides, flesh and dung, all three named. I leave crumbs on my counter after every batch, but this fire leaves nothing on that list.

Enrich sounds like a day to get ahead, baker, but look at the verse. “…you shall humble yourselves and not do any work…” (Leviticus 16:29). You can't enrich anything with your hands in your pockets. The word is humble.

That's not what the verse says, friend. The LORD says, “…on this day atonement will be made for you to cleanse you…” (Leviticus 16:30). The reason given is the cleansing, and this verse says nothing about leaving Egypt. Putting a different event on this date is like setting my oven timer for somebody else's batch. The day is a big deal because of atonement.
